newsitem.title: INDIA: Use of new instruments in risk management - RBI.
newsitem.headline: Use of new instruments in risk management - RBI.

text.p: Following is the full text of a statement issued by the Reserve Bank of India on Friday on the use of new instruments in risk management:

Ever since the burden of covering the exchange risk of FCNR deposits was shifted to banks in 1993, the demand has been voiced that authorised dealers may be accorded the freedom to use derivative productis to manage their foriegn currency assets and liabilities.

The Expert Group on Foreign Exchange Markets in India had also made a recommendation in this regard. It has, therefore, been decided to accept the recommendation and allow authorised dealers, the use of the following instruments to hedge their asset-liability portfolio:
The use of the above instruments would be, inter alia, subject to the following conditions.
I. An appropriate risk management policy envisaging the use of the above instruments should be approved by the top management of the bank.

II. The value of the hedge should not exceed the value of underlying amount and the maturity of the hedge should not exceed the maturity of the underlying. In other words, 'stand alone' transactions should not be initiated. However, in the event of a hedge becoming naked either in full or in part owing to shrinking of the portfolio and other changes in composition, such transactions may be allowed to continue till maturity.
The net cash flows arising out of these transactions should be booked as income/expenditure and would form part of the exchange position.

While the outstanding items need not be subjected to revaluation, those that are not backed by an underlying in the circumstances stated in paragraph 2 (II) above should be marked to market at regular intervals.

Authorised dealers should report details of the above transactions put through, on a quarterly basis in the format which will be prescribed shortly and amendments to the Exchange Control Manual will be advised in due course.

The directions contained in this circular have been issued under Section 73 (3) of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973 (45 of 1973) and contravention or non-observance thereof is subject to the penalties prescribed under the Act.
